sanskrit: sa hi paramagurur bhuvanapatir; dharaṇidharaḥ śamaniyamanidhiḥ śrutivinayanidhir dvijaparamahitas; tava bhavatu gatir harir amarahitaḥ
english: For he is the supreme teacher, the lord of the worlds, the bearer of the earth, the treasury of tranquility and restraint, the treasury of scripture and discipline, the highest benefactor of the twice-born—may Hari, the friend of the gods, be your refuge.

sanskrit: tapasāṃ nidhiḥ sumahatāṃ mahato; yaśasaś ca bhājanam ariṣṭakahā ekāntināṃ śaraṇado 'bhayado; gatido 'stu vaḥ sa makhabhāgaharaḥ
english: He is the treasury of the greatest austerities, the vessel of mighty glory, the slayer of misfortune, the giver of refuge to the single-minded devotees, the bestower of fearlessness—may he who receives his portion of the sacrifice be the granter of your final goal.

sanskrit: triguṇātigaś catuṣpañcadharaḥ; pūrteṣṭayoś ca phalabhāgaharaḥ vidadhāti nityam ajito 'tibalo; gatim ātmagāṃ sukṛtinām ṛṣiṇām
english: Transcending the three qualities, upholder of the four and the five, the receiver of the fruit-share of works of charity and sacrifice—the unconquered one of surpassing strength ever ordains the goal that leads to himself for the virtuous sages.

sanskrit: taṃ lokasākṣiṇam ajaṃ puruṣaṃ; ravivarṇam īśvaragatiṃ bahuśaḥ praṇamadhvam ekamatayo yatayaḥ; salilodbhavo 'pi tam ṛṣiṃ praṇataḥ
english: To him, the witness of the worlds, the unborn Person, sun-hued, the lord's own goal, bow down again and again, O ascetics of single mind; even the lotus-born Brahmā bowed low before that seer.

sanskrit: sa hi lokayonir amṛtasya padaṃ; sūkṣmaṃ purāṇam acalaṃ paramam tat sāṃkhyayogibhir udāradhṛtaṃ; buddhyā yatātmabhir viditaṃ satatam
english: For he is the womb of the worlds, the abode of immortality—subtle, ancient, unmoving, supreme; held high by the followers of Sāṃkhya and Yoga, ever known through intellect by those whose selves are restrained.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca śrutaṃ bhagavatas tasya māhātmyaṃ paramātmanaḥ janma dharmagṛhe caiva naranārāyaṇātmakam mahāvarāhasṛṣṭā ca piṇḍotpattiḥ purātanī
english: Janamejaya said: I have heard the greatness of that blessed Supreme Self—his birth in the house of Dharma in the twofold form of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, and the ancient origin of the earth-mass brought forth by the Great Boar.

sanskrit: pravṛttau ca nivṛttau ca yo yathā parikalpitaḥ sa tathā naḥ śruto brahman kathyamānas tvayānagha
english: How he is ordained in the path of action and in the path of withdrawal—just so have we heard it, O brāhmaṇa, as it was recounted by you, O sinless one.

sanskrit: yac ca tat kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ tvayā hayaśiro mahat havyakavyabhujo viṣṇor udakpūrve mahodadhau tac ca dṛṣṭaṃ bhagavatā brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā
english: And that great Horse-Head of Viṣṇu, the devourer of oblations to gods and ancestors, which you described before as being in the great ocean to the north-east—that too was seen by the blessed Brahmā, the supreme lord.

sanskrit: kiṃ tad utpāditaṃ pūrvaṃ hariṇā lokadhāriṇā rūpaṃ prabhāvamahatām apūrvaṃ dhīmatāṃ vara
english: What was that form, unprecedented among beings of great power, brought forth of old by Hari, the upholder of the worlds, O best of the wise?

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā hi vibudhaśreṣṭham apūrvam amitaujasam tad aśvaśirasaṃ puṇyaṃ brahmā kim akaron mune
english: For when he beheld that holy Horse-Head, the foremost of the gods, unprecedented and of immeasurable might, what did Brahmā do, O sage?

sanskrit: etan naḥ saṃśayaṃ brahman purāṇajñānasaṃbhavam kathayasvottamamate mahāpuruṣanirmitam pāvitāḥ sma tvayā brahman puṇyāṃ kathayatā kathām
english: Resolve this doubt of ours, O brāhmaṇa—a doubt born of ancient lore and fashioned by the Great Person—O you of supreme mind; we have been purified by you, O brāhmaṇa, as you recount this holy tale.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kathayiṣyāmi te sarvaṃ purāṇaṃ vedasaṃmitam jagau yad bhagavān vyāso rājño dharmasutasya vai
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: I shall tell you the whole of it—the ancient tale equal in worth to the Veda, which the blessed Vyāsa sang to the king, the son of Dharma.

sanskrit: śrutvāśvaśiraso mūrtiṃ devasya harimedhasaḥ utpannasaṃśayo rājā tam eva samacodayat
english: Having heard of the Horse-Headed form of the god whose intelligence is Hari, the king, in whom a doubt had arisen, pressed him with a question.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yat tad darśitavān brahmā devaṃ hayaśirodharam kimarthaṃ tat samabhavad vapur devopakalpitam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That god bearing the horse's head whom Brahmā revealed—for what purpose did that body, fashioned by the god, come into being?

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca yat kiṃ cid iha loke vai dehabaddhaṃ viśāṃ pate sarvaṃ pañcabhir āviṣṭaṃ bhūtair īśvarabuddhijaiḥ
english: Vyāsa said: Whatever in this world is bound within a body, O lord of peoples, all of it is pervaded by the five elements, born of the Lord's intelligence.

sanskrit: īśvaro hi jagatsraṣṭā prabhur nārāyaṇo virāṭ bhūtāntarātmā varadaḥ saguṇo nirguṇo 'pi ca bhūtapralayam avyaktaṃ śṛṇuṣva nṛpasattama
english: For the Lord, creator of the world, is the sovereign Nārāyaṇa, the all-pervading; he is the inner Self of beings, the giver of boons, possessed of qualities and yet without qualities. Hear now of the unmanifest dissolution of beings, O best of kings.

sanskrit: dharaṇyām atha līnāyām apsu caikārṇave purā jyotirbhūte jale cāpi līne jyotiṣi cānile
english: When of old the earth had dissolved into the waters, and they into the single ocean; when the water, become fire, had dissolved into light, and the light into wind—

sanskrit: vāyau cākāśasaṃlīne ākāśe ca manonuge vyakte manasi saṃlīne vyakte cāvyaktatāṃ gate
english: when the wind had dissolved into space, and space had followed into mind; when the manifest had dissolved into mind, and the manifest had passed into the unmanifest—

sanskrit: avyakte puruṣaṃ yāte puṃsi sarvagate 'pi ca tama evābhavat sarvaṃ na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: when the unmanifest had gone into the Person, and the Person too into the all-pervading—then there was only darkness, and nothing whatsoever could be discerned.

sanskrit: tamaso brahma saṃbhūtaṃ tamomūlam ṛtātmakam tad viśvabhāvasaṃjñāntaṃ pauruṣīṃ tanum āsthitam
english: From that darkness arose Brahman, rooted in darkness, having truth for its essence; it, ending in the name of universal being, took on a body of the Person.

sanskrit: so 'niruddha iti proktas tat pradhānaṃ pracakṣate tad avyaktam iti jñeyaṃ triguṇaṃ nṛpasattama
english: That is called Aniruddha; that they declare to be the Primordial Nature. It is to be known as the Unmanifest, composed of the three qualities, O best of kings.

sanskrit: vidyāsahāyavān devo viṣvakseno hariḥ prabhuḥ apsv eva śayanaṃ cakre nidrāyogam upāgataḥ jagataś cintayan sṛṣṭiṃ citrāṃ bahuguṇodbhavām
english: The god Viṣvaksena, the lord Hari, accompanied by his power of wisdom, made his couch upon the waters and entered the yoga of sleep, pondering the creation of the world—a wondrous creation arising from manifold qualities.

sanskrit: tasya cintayataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ mahān ātmaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ahaṃkāras tato jāto brahmā śubhacaturmukhaḥ hiraṇyagarbho bhagavān sarvalokapitāmahaḥ
english: As he pondered creation, the Great Principle, called the quality of the Self, arose; from it was born self-consciousness, and thence Brahmā of the four auspicious faces, the blessed Hiraṇyagarbha, grandfather of all the worlds.

sanskrit: padme 'niruddhāt saṃbhūtas tadā padmanibhekṣaṇaḥ sahasrapatre dyutimān upaviṣṭaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Sprung then from Aniruddha upon a lotus, lotus-eyed and radiant, the eternal one sat upon the thousand-petalled flower.

sanskrit: dadṛśe 'dbhutasaṃkāśe lokān āpomayān prabhuḥ sattvasthaḥ parameṣṭhī sa tato bhūtagaṇān sṛjat
english: In that wondrous expanse the lord beheld the worlds made wholly of water; abiding in goodness, the supreme one then brought forth the hosts of beings.

sanskrit: pūrvam eva ca padmasya patre sūryāṃśusaprabhe nārāyaṇakṛtau bindū apām āstāṃ guṇottarau
english: And even before that, upon the petal of the lotus, bright as the sun's rays, there were two drops of water made by Nārāyaṇa, surpassing in their qualities.

sanskrit: tāv apaśyat sa bhagavān anādinidhano 'cyutaḥ ekas tatrābhavad bindur madhvābho ruciraprabhaḥ
english: The blessed one, without beginning or end, the unfallen, beheld those two; one drop there was the color of honey, of lovely radiance.

sanskrit: sa tāmaso madhur jātas tadā nārāyaṇājñayā kaṭhinas tv aparo binduḥ kaiṭabho rājasas tu saḥ
english: That one, born of darkness, became Madhu by the command of Nārāyaṇa; the other drop, hard, born of passion, became Kaiṭabha.

sanskrit: tāv abhyadhāvatāṃ śreṣṭhau tamorajaguṇānvitau balavantau gadāhastau padmanālānusāriṇau
english: Those two mighty foremost ones, endowed with the qualities of darkness and passion, maces in hand, rushed forth, making their way along the stalk of the lotus.

sanskrit: dadṛśāte 'ravindasthaṃ brahmāṇam amitaprabham sṛjantaṃ prathamaṃ vedāṃś caturaś cāruvigrahān
english: They beheld Brahmā of immeasurable splendor, seated upon the lotus, first bringing forth the four Vedas of lovely form.

sanskrit: tato vigrahavantau tau vedān dṛṣṭvāsurottamau sahasā jagṛhatur vedān brahmaṇaḥ paśyatas tadā
english: Then those two foremost of demons, having taken bodily form, seeing the Vedas, suddenly seized them as Brahmā looked on.

sanskrit: atha tau dānavaśreṣṭhau vedān gṛhya sanātanān rasāṃ viviśatus tūrṇam udakpūrve mahodadhau
english: Then those two foremost of the Dānavas, having seized the eternal Vedas, swiftly entered the netherworld in the great ocean to the north-east.

sanskrit: tato hṛteṣu vedeṣu brahmā kaśmalam āviśat tato vacanam īśānaṃ prāha vedair vinākṛtaḥ
english: Then, when the Vedas had been stolen, Brahmā fell into despair; bereft of the Vedas, he spoke these words to the Lord.

sanskrit: vedā me paramaṃ cakṣur vedā me paramaṃ balam vedā me paramaṃ dhāma vedā me brahma cottamam
english: "The Vedas are my supreme eye, the Vedas are my supreme strength; the Vedas are my supreme abode, the Vedas are my highest Brahman."

sanskrit: mama vedā hṛtāḥ sarve dānavābhyāṃ balād itaḥ andhakārā hi me lokā jātā vedair vinākṛtāḥ vedān ṛte hi kiṃ kuryāṃ lokān vai sraṣṭum udyataḥ
english: "All my Vedas have been carried off from here by force by the two Dānavas; bereft of the Vedas, my worlds have become wrapped in darkness. What can I do without the Vedas, intent as I am upon creating the worlds?"

sanskrit: aho bata mahad duḥkhaṃ vedanāśanajaṃ mama prāptaṃ dunoti hṛdayaṃ tīvraśokāya randhayan
english: "Alas, a great sorrow born of the loss of the Vedas has come upon me; it torments my heart, rending it open to fierce grief."

sanskrit: ko hi śokārṇave magnaṃ mām ito 'dya samuddharet vedāṃs tān ānayen naṣṭān kasya cāhaṃ priyo bhave
english: "Who shall today lift me, sunk in this ocean of grief, out of it, and bring back those lost Vedas? To whom shall I become dear?"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ bhāṣamāṇasya brahmaṇo nṛpasattama hareḥ stotrārtham udbhūtā buddhir buddhimatāṃ vara tato jagau paraṃ japyaṃ sāñjalipragrahaḥ prabhuḥ
english: As Brahmā spoke thus, O best of kings, O foremost of the wise, the thought arose in him to praise Hari; then the lord, with hands joined in reverence, intoned a supreme hymn.

sanskrit: namas te brahmahṛdaya namas te mama pūrvaja lokādya bhuvanaśreṣṭha sāṃkhyayoganidhe vibho
english: "Homage to you, O heart of Brahman; homage to you, my forefather; O first of the worlds, best of all beings, treasury of Sāṃkhya and Yoga, O all-pervading one."

sanskrit: vyaktāvyaktakarācintya kṣemaṃ panthānam āsthita viśvabhuk sarvabhūtānām antarātmann ayonija
english: "O inconceivable maker of the manifest and unmanifest, you who abide upon the path of well-being, devourer of the universe, inner Self of all beings, O you who are born of no womb!"

sanskrit: ahaṃ prasādajas tubhyaṃ lokadhāmne svayaṃbhuve tvatto me mānasaṃ janma prathamaṃ dvijapūjitam
english: "I am born of your grace, to you the abode of the worlds, the self-existent. From you came my first birth, born of the mind, honored by the twice-born."

sanskrit: cākṣuṣaṃ vai dvitīyaṃ me janma cāsīt purātanam tvatprasādāc ca me janma tṛtīyaṃ vācikaṃ mahat
english: "My second birth of old was from the eye; and by your grace my third great birth was from speech."

sanskrit: tvattaḥ śravaṇajaṃ cāpi caturthaṃ janma me vibho nāsikyaṃ cāpi me janma tvattaḥ pañcamam ucyate
english: "From you, too, came my fourth birth, born of the ear, O all-pervading one; and my birth from the nose is called the fifth, again from you."

sanskrit: aṇḍajaṃ cāpi me janma tvattaḥ ṣaṣṭhaṃ vinirmitam idaṃ ca saptamaṃ janma padmajaṃ me 'mitaprabha
english: "And my birth from the egg, the sixth, was fashioned by you; and this is my seventh birth, born of the lotus, O you of measureless splendor."

sanskrit: sarge sarge hy ahaṃ putras tava triguṇavarjitaḥ prathitaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣa pradhānaguṇakalpitaḥ
english: "In creation after creation I am your son, free of the three qualities, renowned, O lotus-eyed one, fashioned from the qualities of Primordial Nature."

sanskrit: tvam īśvarasvabhāvaś ca svayaṃbhūḥ puruṣottamaḥ tvayā vinirmito 'haṃ vai vedacakṣur vayotigaḥ
english: "You are the very nature of the Lord, the self-existent, the supreme Person; by you was I fashioned, having the Vedas for my eye, surpassing all age."

sanskrit: te me vedā hṛtāś cakṣur andho jāto 'smi jāgṛhi dadasva cakṣuṣī mahyaṃ priyo 'haṃ te priyo 'si me
english: "Those Vedas, my eye, have been stolen; I have become blind. Awake! Restore to me my two eyes. I am dear to you, and you are dear to me."

sanskrit: evaṃ stutaḥ sa bhagavān puruṣaḥ sarvatomukhaḥ jahau nidrām atha tadā vedakāryārtham udyataḥ aiśvareṇa prayogeṇa dvitīyāṃ tanum āsthitaḥ
english: Thus praised, the blessed Person, facing in every direction, then forsook his sleep, intent upon the task of the Vedas, and by his sovereign power took on a second body.

sanskrit: sunāsikena kāyena bhūtvā candraprabhas tadā kṛtvā hayaśiraḥ śubhraṃ vedānām ālayaṃ prabhuḥ
english: With a body finely formed and fair as the moon, the lord then made the white horse's head, the abode of the Vedas.

sanskrit: tasya mūrdhā samabhavad dyauḥ sanakṣatratārakā keśāś cāsyābhavan dīrghā raver aṃśusamaprabhāḥ
english: His head became the heavens with their constellations and stars, and his long hairs became bright as the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: karṇāv ākāśapātāle lalāṭaṃ bhūtadhāriṇī gaṅgā sarasvatī puṇyā bhruvāv āstāṃ mahānadī
english: His two ears were the sky and the nether regions, his brow the earth that bears all beings; the holy Gaṅgā and Sarasvatī, the great rivers, were his two eyebrows.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣī somasūryau te nāsā saṃdhyā punaḥ smṛtā oṃkāras tv atha saṃskāro vidyuj jihvā ca nirmitā
english: His two eyes were the moon and the sun; his nose was held to be the twilight; the syllable Oṃ was his ritual consecration, and lightning was made his tongue.

sanskrit: dantāś ca pitaro rājan somapā iti viśrutāḥ goloko brahmalokaś ca oṣṭhāv āstāṃ mahātmanaḥ grīvā cāsyābhavad rājan kālarātrir guṇottarā
english: His teeth, O king, were the ancestors known as the drinkers of soma; the world of cows and the world of Brahmā were the lips of the great one; and his neck, O king, was the Night of Time, surpassing in its qualities.

sanskrit: etad dhayaśiraḥ kṛtvā nānāmūrtibhir āvṛtam antardadhe sa viśveśo viveśa ca rasāṃ prabhuḥ
english: Having made this horse's head, wrapped about with manifold forms, the lord of all, the sovereign, vanished and entered the netherworld.

sanskrit: rasāṃ punaḥ praviṣṭaś ca yogaṃ paramam āsthitaḥ śaikṣaṃ svaraṃ samāsthāya om iti prāsṛjat svaram
english: Having entered the netherworld once more and taken up the supreme yoga, he, assuming the disciplined tone of the science of recitation, sent forth the sound Oṃ.

sanskrit: sa svaraḥ sānunādī ca sarvagaḥ snigdha eva ca babhūvāntarmahībhūtaḥ sarvabhūtaguṇoditaḥ
english: That sound, resonant and far-reaching, all-pervading and tender, became hidden within the earth, arising from the qualities of all beings.

sanskrit: tatas tāv asurau kṛtvā vedān samayabandhanān rasātale vinikṣipya yataḥ śabdas tato drutau
english: Then those two Asuras, having bound the Vedas by a pact and laid them down in the netherworld, rushed toward the place from which the sound came.

sanskrit: etasminn antare rājan devo hayaśirodharaḥ jagrāha vedān akhilān rasātalagatān hariḥ prādāc ca brahmaṇe bhūyas tataḥ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ
english: In that interval, O king, the god Hari, bearing the horse's head, seized all the Vedas that had been left in the netherworld and gave them back to Brahmā, then returned to his own nature.

sanskrit: sthāpayitvā hayaśira udakpūrve mahodadhau vedānām ālayaś cāpi babhūvāśvaśirās tataḥ
english: Having set the horse's head in the great ocean to the north-east, the Horse-Headed one thus became the abode of the Vedas.

sanskrit: atha kiṃ cid apaśyantau dānavau madhukaiṭabhau punar ājagmatus tatra vegitau paśyatāṃ ca tau yatra vedā vinikṣiptās tat sthānaṃ śūnyam eva ca
english: Then the two Dānavas, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, seeing nothing, came rushing back to that place; and they beheld that the spot where the Vedas had been laid was empty.

sanskrit: tata uttamam āsthāya vegaṃ balavatāṃ varau punar uttasthatuḥ śīghraṃ rasānām ālayāt tadā dadṛśāte ca puruṣaṃ tam evādikaraṃ prabhum
english: Then, taking on their utmost speed, those two foremost of the strong rose up swiftly again from the abode of the waters and beheld that very Person, the lord, the first maker.

sanskrit: śvetaṃ candraviśuddhābham aniruddhatanau sthitam bhūyo 'py amitavikrāntaṃ nidrāyogam upāgatam
english: White, gleaming pure as the moon, abiding in the body of Aniruddha, of immeasurable valor, he had once more entered the yoga of sleep.

sanskrit: ātmapramāṇaracite apām upari kalpite śayane nāgabhogāḍhye jvālāmālāsamāvṛte
english: He lay upon a couch fashioned to his own measure, set above the waters, made rich with the coils of the serpent and wreathed about with garlands of flame.

sanskrit: niṣkalmaṣeṇa sattvena saṃpannaṃ ruciraprabham taṃ dṛṣṭvā dānavendrau tau mahāhāsam amuñcatām
english: Endowed with stainless goodness and of lovely radiance—seeing him, those two lords of the Dānavas burst into great laughter.

sanskrit: ūcatuś ca samāviṣṭau rajasā tamasā ca tau ayaṃ sa puruṣaḥ śvetaḥ śete nidrām upāgataḥ
english: And those two, possessed by passion and darkness, said: "This is that white Person who lies here sunk in sleep."

sanskrit: anena nūnaṃ vedānāṃ kṛtam āharaṇaṃ rasāt kasyaiṣa ko nu khalv eṣa kiṃ ca svapiti bhogavān
english: "Surely it is by him that the Vedas were carried off from the netherworld. Whose is he? Who indeed is this? And why does he sleep in such luxury?"

sanskrit: ity uccāritavākyau tau bodhayām āsatur harim yuddhārthinau tu vijñāya vibuddhaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
english: Having uttered these words, the two roused Hari; and the supreme Person, awaking, perceived that they sought battle.

sanskrit: nirīkṣya cāsurendrau tau tato yuddhe mano dadhe atha yuddhaṃ samabhavat tayor nārāyaṇasya ca
english: And gazing upon those two lords of the Asuras, he set his mind upon battle; then there arose a war between the two of them and Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: rajastamoviṣṭatanū tāv ubhau madhukaiṭabhau brahmaṇopacitiṃ kurvañ jaghāna madhusūdanaḥ
english: Those two, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, their bodies possessed by passion and darkness—the slayer of Madhu killed them, doing a service of recompense to Brahmā.

sanskrit: tatas tayor vadhenāśu vedāpaharaṇena ca śokāpanayanaṃ cakre brahmaṇaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
english: Then, by the slaying of those two and by the recovery of the Vedas, the supreme Person swiftly dispelled the grief of Brahmā.

sanskrit: tataḥ parivṛto brahmā hatārir vedasatkṛtaḥ nirmame sa tadā lokān kṛtsnān sthāvarajaṅgamān
english: Then Brahmā, his foes slain and honored by the restoring of the Vedas, attended by his retinue, created all the worlds, both the moving and the unmoving.

sanskrit: dattvā pitāmahāyāgryāṃ buddhiṃ lokavisargikīm tatraivāntardadhe devo yata evāgato hariḥ
english: Having granted to the Grandfather the foremost wisdom for the bringing-forth of the worlds, the god Hari vanished thereupon into the very place from which he had come.

sanskrit: tau dānavau harir hatvā kṛtvā hayaśiras tanum punaḥ pravṛttidharmārthaṃ tām eva vidadhe tanum
english: Having slain those two Dānavas and made the horse-headed body, Hari, for the sake of the dharma of activity, again established that very body.

sanskrit: evam eṣa mahābhāgo babhūvāśvaśirā hariḥ paurāṇam etad ākhyātaṃ rūpaṃ varadam aiśvaram
english: Thus did this greatly blessed Hari become the Horse-Headed one; this ancient form, boon-granting and sovereign, has now been told.

sanskrit: yo hy etad brāhmaṇo nityaṃ śṛṇuyād dhārayeta vā na tasyādhyayanaṃ nāśam upagacchet kadā cana
english: For that brāhmaṇa who should ever hear this or hold it in memory—his learning would never come to ruin at any time.

sanskrit: ārādhya tapasogreṇa devaṃ hayaśirodharam pāñcālena kramaḥ prāpto rāmeṇa pathi deśite
english: Having propitiated by fierce austerity the god who bears the horse's head, the Pāñcāla attained the method, and Rāma along the path that was pointed out.

sanskrit: etad dhayaśiro rājann ākhyānaṃ tava kīrtitam purāṇaṃ vedasamitaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: This tale of the Horse-Head, O king, has been recounted to you—the ancient story equal in worth to the Veda, about which you questioned me.

sanskrit: yāṃ yām icchet tanuṃ devaḥ kartuṃ kāryavidhau kva cit tāṃ tāṃ kuryād vikurvāṇaḥ svayam ātmānam ātmanā
english: Whatever body the god might wish to make at any time in the ordering of his work, that body he would make, transforming his very self by himself.

sanskrit: eṣa vedanidhiḥ śrīmān eṣa vai tapaso nidhiḥ eṣa yogaś ca sāṃkhyaṃ ca brahma cāgryaṃ harir vibhuḥ
english: This glorious one is the treasury of the Vedas; this indeed is the treasury of austerity; this is Yoga and Sāṃkhya and the foremost Brahman—Hari, the all-pervading lord.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇaparā vedā yajñā nārāyaṇātmakāḥ tapo nārāyaṇaparaṃ nārāyaṇaparā gatiḥ
english: The Vedas have Nārāyaṇa for their goal; the sacrifices have Nārāyaṇa for their essence; austerity has Nārāyaṇa as its highest aim; Nārāyaṇa is the supreme destination.
